title: urn:qauth:ia:upstream:v1-rc.0
description: The person picks one of the realm’s upstream identity providers: generic OpenID Connect, or an AuthMethod plugin. It is offered beside the `identifier` step, before anyone is named, alike for every account (ADR-017 Decision 4); on the sign-in to the account an upstream identity joins (`upstream_link`), the provider being linked is left out (#1080). An answer names one provider of the list; the answer’s result is a redirect to the provider (`result: redirect`, or `303` to it for a form post). The provider sends the browser back to `/upstream/<provider>/callback` on the realm host, which checks the answer against the transaction kept server-side for this interaction and its flow cookie, signs in the account that holds that upstream identity, or, for an identity no account holds, asks at the `upstream_link` step whether it starts a new account or joins an existing one, and continues the interaction (on the sign-in to the account an identity joins, an identity no account holds signs in to nothing and creates nothing): the next step’s ceremony page, or the final redirect. A sign-in through a provider ranks with the password in the downgrade rule, below a passkey (ADR-017 Decision 4), and adds no `amr` value. A provider an operator hides is not listed here and stays reachable through the authorization request’s `qauth_upstream` parameter. When the provider does not sign the person in, its callback sends the browser back to the ceremony page, nothing goes to the client, and this step is the current one again, with the other ways in as its alternatives, its `error` and the provider in `error_provider` (#1081): `provider_declined`, the person cancelled or refused at the provider (OAuth `access_denied`); `provider_error`, the provider answered another error. An answer naming a provider that cannot be started is refused with `provider_unavailable`. Any other failure of the callback, a provider switched off before its answer came back among them, is an error page with the request’s trace id. Works without JavaScript: each provider is a button of a plain form post.

providers.description: The realm’s upstream identity providers, in the order the screen shows them.

provider.description: The provider’s name, which the answer names.

name.description: The provider’s name as the operator set it, for its button.

icon.description: An absolute `https` URL on the realm origin of a PNG icon for the button. Nothing supplies one yet (#714).

error_provider.description: With an `error`, the provider it is about (#1081): the one the person picked, which did not sign them in or could not be started. It may be one the list does not show, such as a provider the operator hides that the authorization request routed to. Absent without an `error`.

name.description: The provider’s name as the operator set it, for the screen’s text.

provider.description: The `provider` of the entry the person picked.

error.description: Why the last answer was refused. A closed set.

amr.description: The RFC 8176 `amr` values a successful answer adds to the transaction: none, because the step proves no authenticator.
